--- title: "[simulate_competing_risks()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Generate synthetic competing-risks data from a latent-Weibull model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_simulate.py#L67-L264){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate_competing_risks( n=500, n_causes=2, *, shapes=None, scales=None, censoring_scale=1.5, n_covariates=0, coef=None, states=None, seed=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each cause has its own Weibull distribution with specified shape and scale parameters. For each subject, a latent event time is drawn independently for every cause, and the cause with the shortest latent time is the one observed. An independent censoring time is drawn from a Weibull(1, scale) distribution (i.e., exponential). If the censoring time is shortest, the subject is censored. When covariates are requested, cause-specific proportional hazards are applied: the Weibull scale for cause $k$ is adjusted as $b_k \cdot \exp(-\mathbf{x}^\top \boldsymbol{\beta}_k / a_k)$, where $a_k$ and $b_k$ are the shape and scale for cause $k$. Covariates are drawn from a standard normal distribution. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[500]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of subjects (default 500). [n_causes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of competing event types (default 2). [shapes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, ...] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Weibull shape parameter for each cause. Length must equal `n_causes`. Defaults to `(1.0, 1.5, ...)` cycling through `[1.0, 1.5, 0.8]`. A shape of 1.0 gives an exponential (constant hazard). Values above 1 give increasing hazard. Values below 1 give decreasing hazard. [scales]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, ...] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Weibull scale parameter for each cause. Length must equal `n_causes`. Defaults to 10.0 for every cause. [censoring_scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.5]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Controls censoring intensity. The censoring time is drawn from an exponential distribution with scale equal to `censoring_scale` times the mean latent event time. Larger values produce less censoring. Set to `None` or `0` to disable censoring entirely. Default is 1.5, which gives roughly 20-30% censoring depending on the shape/scale configuration. [n_covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of covariates to generate (default 0). When positive, standard-normal covariates are drawn and cause-specific proportional-hazards effects are applied. [coef]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Coefficient matrix of shape `(n_covariates, n_causes)` for the proportional-hazards effect on each cause. When `None` (default), coefficients are drawn from Uniform(-0.5, 0.5).Ignored when `n_covariates=0`. [states]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[str, ...] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Names for each cause (e.g., `("relapse", "death")`). Length must equal `n_causes`. Defaults to `("cause1", "cause2", ...)`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [SimulatedCompetingRisks]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A dataclass with `surv` (the multi-state `Surv` response), `covariates` (the covariate matrix or `None`), `latent_times` (per-cause latent times), and `censoring_time`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Generate a simple two-cause competing-risks dataset and fit an Aalen-Johansen estimator: ::: {#476c17b9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw sim = gw.simulate_competing_risks(n=300, n_causes=2, seed=42) sim.surv ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Surv(type=mright, n=300, events=171, states=('cause1', 'cause2')) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#bdfde2d1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} aj = gw.AalenJohansen().fit(sim.surv) aj ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` AalenJohansen (Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence) states: cause1, cause2 n = 300 final CIF cause1 0.5327 cause2 0.4673 ``` ::: ::: Generate data with covariates for a Fine-Gray model: ::: {#0e062158 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} sim = gw.simulate_competing_risks( n=500, n_causes=2, n_covariates=3, states=("relapse", "death"), seed=99, ) fg = gw.FineGray(cause="relapse").fit(sim.surv, covariates=sim.covariates) gw.tidy(fg, format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Control the event-time distribution and censoring rate: ::: {#f6ca3071 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np # Cause 1: increasing hazard (shape > 1), Cause 2: constant hazard sim = gw.simulate_competing_risks( n=1000, n_causes=2, shapes=(2.0, 1.0), scales=(15.0, 10.0), censoring_scale=0.8, # heavier censoring seed=7, ) # Check the censoring fraction frac_censored = (sim.surv.status == 0).mean() print(f"Censored: {frac_censored:.1%}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Censored: 60.1% ``` ::: :::
